questions.stem: In the context of optical phenomena, what causes the formation of a mirage in a desert on a hot summer day?

options.option_text: Total Internal Reflection of light due to atmospheric refraction
Dispersion of light by sand particles
Scattering of light by the hot atmosphere
Interference of light waves near the ground

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: A mirage is an optical illusion (like seeing a pool of water on a hot road). It happens because the sand/road gets extremely hot, heating the layer of air directly above it. Hot air is less dense (lower refractive index) than the cooler air higher up. As light from the sky travels downward through increasingly hotter/less dense layers of air, it bends (refracts) further away from the normal until it hits the critical angle and undergoes Total Internal Reflection (TIR), bending back up into the observer's eye. The brain interprets this light coming from the ground as a reflection off a pool of water.
DECOY BUSTING: Dispersion causes rainbows. Scattering causes the blue sky and red sunsets. Interference causes the rainbow colors on an oil slick or soap bubble.
EXAM INSIGHT: In extremely cold polar regions, the opposite happens: a layer of extremely cold dense air sits on the ground with warmer air above it. This causes a 'Looming' mirage, where ships appear to float upside down in the sky.

questions.stem: Which electromagnetic wave is primarily responsible for the heating effect of the sun and is utilized in devices like night-vision goggles?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Infrared (IR) radiation lies just beyond the red end of the visible light spectrum. It is essentially heat radiation. All warm objects (including human bodies) emit infrared radiation. Night-vision goggles and thermal imaging cameras work by detecting these infrared emissions, allowing us to "see" heat in total darkness.
DECOY BUSTING: Ultraviolet (UV) rays cause sunburns and are used in water purifiers. X-Rays penetrate soft tissue for medical imaging. Microwaves are used in radar and cooking.
EXAM INSIGHT: TV remote controls also use tiny infrared LEDs to send signals to the television.

questions.stem: When a ray of white light passes through a glass prism, it splits into a spectrum of seven colors. Which color bends (deviates) the MOST?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The splitting of white light is called Dispersion. When light enters a denser medium (like glass), different colors travel at slightly different speeds because they have different wavelengths. Red light has the longest wavelength, travels the fastest in glass, and therefore bends the LEAST. Violet light has the shortest wavelength, travels the slowest, and therefore bends the MOST.
DECOY BUSTING: Red is at the top of the spectrum (least bent). Violet is at the bottom (most bent). Think of the acronym VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) from bottom to top.
EXAM INSIGHT: This exact same principle causes rainbows when sunlight passes through spherical raindrops (which act like tiny prisms) suspended in the air after a shower.
